title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection methods only work at the document level (or on narrow, task-specific token tasks such as spell checking), so they cannot localize which tokens in a text are anomalous. The paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection, releases three token-annotated benchmarks (SMS_Spam with injected character corruption, Restaurant Review semantic anomalies, Grammar errors), and proposes TokenCore, which builds a memory bank of normal word-level token embeddings (BERT-base-uncased embeddings aggregated by element-wise max pooling over subwords) and scores each test token by its nearest-neighbor distance, aggregating token scores by mean for document-level scores. TokenCore achieves the best average token-level AUROC (0.7145) and document-level AUROC (0.7335) among 7 methods, ranking first at token level on Review (0.8271) and Grammar (0.6371) and at document level on Review (0.9594), while ECOD/iForest remain better on the character-corruption SMS_Spam token-level task.

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction of claim C1: TokenCore's token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (0.6371, tolerance ±0.02 absolute). We clone the authors' repo, keep TokenCore.py/align.py/json_to_npy.py verbatim, and rebuild only the missing driver that Demo.ipynb used to hide: read the released grammar annotations (data/grammar_correction_labeled.json and data/grammar.npy), build the 300-document corpus (270 normal / 30 anomalous, R10), take 50% of the normal documents as the memory-bank training set (R6, A8), run BERT-base-uncased over the remaining normal + anomalous documents, max-pool subword embeddings into word units aligned with the gold word-level token labels (Eq. 1, R2/R9, A3/A4), fit the authors' TextCore memory bank on normal-training token embeddings only (R3, A2), score every test token by Euclidean nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 2, R4, A1/A9), and compute pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC plus the mean-aggregated document-level scores (Eq. 3, R5, A5). The paper value is a single split-free number, so the only real drift risk is split randomness on 300 short documents; we therefore report a primary seeded run plus a small multi-seed spread so the ±0.02 band can be interpreted. Only the Grammar dataset is needed for C1, but the same driver is written so that running it on restaurant_review / sms_spam later costs nothing extra.

    1| # TokenCore
    2| 
    3| Official code and datasets for the paper
    4| **[Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection](https://huggingface.co/papers/2601.13644)** (WWW '26).
    5| 
    6| TokenCore is a memory-bank method for **token-level text anomaly detection**: instead of only flagging whole documents as anomalous, it localizes *which specific tokens* are anomalous. It builds a memory bank of normal token embeddings and scores each test token by its distance to the nearest normal neighbor, then aggregates token scores to obtain document-level scores.
    7| 
    8| ## Datasets
    9| 
   10| The three benchmark datasets are hosted on the Hugging Face Hub:
   11| 
   12| 👉 **[https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD)**

   16| | Dataset | Anomaly type | Documents | Anomalies | Rate |
   17| |---|---|---|---|---|
   18| | SMS Spam | Character-level (corrupted sequences) | 4,518 | 393 | 8.7% |
   19| | Restaurant Review | Semantic (negative sentiment) | 1,100 | 50 | 4.5% |
   20| | Grammar Correction | Grammatical errors | 300 | 30 | 10% |

"""Reproduce TokenCore (arXiv:2601.13644) on the Grammar benchmark (claims C1/C2 + doc-level).

Pipeline (from the authors' Demo.ipynb, rebuilt as a script):
  1. Load the released grammar annotations (repo/data/grammar.npy).
  2. Split: 50% of normal documents -> training; rest normal + all anomalous -> test (Sec 6.1).
  3. BERT-base-uncased contextual embeddings, last hidden state; element-wise MAX pooling
     over subwords -> word-level embeddings (paper Eq. 1, authors' align.py).
  4. Memory bank = all normal-training token embeddings; token score = distance to nearest
     neighbor (Eq. 2, authors' TokenCore.py, Euclidean via sklearn NearestNeighbors).
  5. Document score = mean of token scores (Eq. 3).
  6. Token-level and document-level AUROC / AUPRC on the test set.
"""
import argparse, json, os, sys, time
import numpy as np
import torch

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "repo"))

from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score
from TokenCore import TokenCore  # authors' implementation, unmodified

MODEL_NAME = "bert-base-uncased"
DATA = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "repo", "data", "grammar.npy")
MAX_LEN = 128


def load_grammar(smoke=False):
    d = np.load(DATA, allow_pickle=True).item()
    tokens, labels = d["tokens"], d["labels"]
    assert len(tokens) == 300, len(tokens)
    doc_labels = [1 if any(l) else 0 for l in labels]
    n_anom = sum(doc_labels)
    assert n_anom == 30, n_anom  # 10% anomaly rate (R10)
    if smoke:
        norm = [i for i, y in enumerate(doc_labels) if y == 0][:8]
        anom = [i for i, y in enumerate(doc_labels) if y == 1][:2]
        keep = norm + anom
        tokens = [tokens[i] for i in keep]
        labels = [labels[i] for i in keep]
        doc_labels = [doc_labels[i] for i in keep]
    return tokens, labels, doc_labels


def split_50(doc_labels, seed):
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    norm_idx = np.array([i for i, y in enumerate(doc_labels) if y == 0])
    rng.shuffle(norm_idx)

"""Reproduce TokenCore (arXiv:2601.13644) on the Grammar benchmark (claims C1/C2 + doc-level).

Uses the AUTHORS' OWN pipeline verbatim (repo/align.py extract_word_embeddings +
repo/TokenCore.py), exactly as called in repo/demo.ipynb:
  - bert-base-cased (the checkpoint actually used in demo.ipynb; the paper text says
    uncased, so this is recorded as an assumption),
  - per-sentence forward pass, no padding, last hidden state,
  - element-wise MAX pooling over subwords -> word-level embeddings (Eq. 1),
  - memory bank = all normal-training token embeddings; token score = Euclidean distance
    to nearest neighbor (Eq. 2),
  - document score = mean of token scores (Eq. 3),
  - split: 50% of normal documents -> training; rest normal + all anomalous -> test.
"""
import argparse, contextlib, io, json, os, sys, time
import numpy as np

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(ROOT, "repo"))

from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score
from align import extract_word_embeddings   # authors' embedding extraction, unmodified
from TokenCore import TokenCore             # authors' detector, unmodified

MODEL_NAME = "bert-base-cased"  # as in demo.ipynb (paper text says uncased; see assumption)
DATA = os.path.join(ROOT, "repo", "data", "grammar.npy")


def load_grammar(smoke=False):
    d = np.load(DATA, allow_pickle=True).item()
    tokens, labels = d["tokens"], d["labels"]
    assert len(tokens) == 300, len(tokens)
    doc_labels = [1 if any(l) else 0 for l in labels]
    n_anom = sum(doc_labels)
    assert n_anom == 30, n_anom  # 10% anomaly rate (R10)
    if smoke:
        norm = [i for i, y in enumerate(doc_labels) if y == 0][:8]
        anom = [i for i, y in enumerate(doc_labels) if y == 1][:2]
        keep = norm + anom
        tokens = [tokens[i] for i in keep]
        labels = [labels[i] for i in keep]
        doc_labels = [doc_labels[i] for i in keep]
    return tokens, labels, doc_labels


def split_50(doc_labels, seed):
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    norm_idx = np.array([i for i, y in enumerate(doc_labels) if y == 0])
    rng.shuffle(norm_idx)
    half = len(norm_idx) // 2
    train_idx = set(norm_idx[:half].tolist())
    test_idx = [i for i in range(len(doc_labels)) if i not in train_idx]
    return sorted(train_idx), test_idx


def run_once(seed, tokens, labels, doc_labels):
    train_idx, test_idx = split_50(doc_labels, seed)
    z_te = [labels[i] for i in test_idx]

    # authors' path, verbatim call signature from demo.ipynb (silence verbose prints)
    buf = io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
        tr = extract_word_embeddings(model=None, tokenizer=None,
                                     all_tokens=[tokens[i] for i in train_idx],
                                     all_labels=[labels[i] for i in train_idx],
                                     model_name=MODEL_NAME, local_cache_dir=None, device="cpu")
        te = extract_word_embeddings(model=None, tokenizer=None,
                                     all_tokens=[tokens[i] for i in test_idx],
                                     all_labels=z_te,
                                     model_name=MODEL_NAME, local_cache_dir=None, device="cpu")

    # alignment assertion: one scored word unit per gold token label, per test doc
    mism = [(i, len(s), len(l)) for i, (s, l) in enumerate(zip(te, z_te)) if len(s) != len(l)]
    assert not mism, f"word-unit/label misalignment in test docs: {mism}"

    X_train = np.array([it["embedding"] for s in tr for it in s])
    X_test = np.array([it["embedding"] for s in te for it in s])
    z_test = np.array([it["label"] for s in te for it in s])
    z_doc = np.array([doc_labels[i] for i in test_idx])
    assert X_train.shape[1] == 768
    assert sum(sum(l) for l in (labels[i] for i in train_idx)) == 0  # normal-only bank (R3)

    det = TokenCore()  # k=1 nearest neighbor (Eq. 2)
    det.fit(X_train)
    score = det.decision_function(X_test)

    doc_scores, off = [], 0
    for s in te:
        doc_scores.append(float(score[off:off + len(s)].mean()))  # Eq. 3
        off += len(s)

    rng = np.random.RandomState(123)
    return {
        "seed": seed,
        "token_auroc": float(roc_auc_score(z_test, score)),
        "token_auprc": float(average_precision_score(z_test, score)),
        "doc_auroc": float(roc_auc_score(z_doc, doc_scores)),
        "doc_auprc": float(average_precision_score(z_doc, doc_scores)),
        "random_control_token_auroc": float(roc_auc_score(z_test, rng.rand(len(z_test)))),
        "n_train_docs": len(train_idx), "n_test_docs": len(test_idx),
        "n_test_docs_anomalous": int(z_doc.sum()),
        "n_bank_tokens": int(len(X_train)), "n_test_tokens": int(len(X_test)),
        "n_positive_tokens": int(z_test.sum()),
    }


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    t0 = time.time()
    os.makedirs("results", exist_ok=True)

    tokens, labels, doc_labels = load_grammar(smoke=args.smoke)
    print(f"docs={len(tokens)} anomalous={sum(doc_labels)} "
          f"tokens={sum(len(l) for l in labels)} pos_tokens={sum(sum(l) for l in labels)}")

    r = run_once(args.seed, tokens, labels, doc_labels)

    metrics = {
        "metric": "AUROC",
        "value": r["token_auroc"],
        "dataset": "Grammar (Grammar Correction)",
        "split": "test = 50% of documents (normal + anomalous); token-level scoring; split seed 0",
        "config": {
            "backbone": "bert-base-cased, last hidden state (checkpoint used by authors' demo.ipynb; paper text says uncased)",
            "subword_pooling": "element-wise max over subwords (Eq. 1, authors' align.py)",
            "memory_bank": "all normal-training token embeddings (R3)",
            "token_score": "Euclidean nearest-neighbor distance, k=1 (Eq. 2, authors' TokenCore.py)",
